note: Track modes, step 2: Dorian built from the minor pentatonic scale by adding the 2nd and the major 6th, the 6th tapped against the root over a drone, then aimed for over a Dorian backing track whose two chords are counted the long way as chord tokens. The key is moves (any key): the old Key selector is gone, the key is named as {{=key}}, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: Dorian: the minor pentatonic plus two notes
exercise.why: Dorian is the minor pentatonic scale with the 2nd and the major 6th added, and the 6th is the note that sets it apart from natural minor, so hearing that note against the root is hearing Dorian.

cells.text:
The staff below shows {{=key}} Dorian. The plain notes are the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale, and the ringed {{2}} and {{6}} are the two notes Dorian adds.
Tap up the scale from {{1}}, then tap {{5}}, {{6}} and {{5}} to hear the major 6th beside its neighbour.
Practice until you can hum {{6}} before you tap it.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. Tap {{1}}, the ringed {{6}} and {{1}} on the staff under it, then tap short lines of your own that keep coming back to {{6}}.
Practice until {{6}} sounds bright against the drone every time you land on it.

{{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:IV7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track: the two chords, round and round. Tap lines of your own on the staff under it, and land on the ringed {{6}} when {{chord:IV7}} comes: {{6}} is that chord's 3rd.
Practice until the {{6}} lands with the chord without you watching the chord boxes.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the ringed note is still the {{6}}, the 3rd of the 4th chord.
